description:
This is so simple to make at home, Alcohol free blueberry extract using vegetable glycerin. 

I've never had an issue using normal vanilla extract in backing etc, my kid loves vanilla flavours. Most extracts have been makde with alcohol (ethanol) since they've been available in the stores. If you are the person who doesn't want to use these alcohol based extracts, this video will be for you. 

The glycerin has the same freezing point supression as alcohol too so using it in your ice cream or gelato is amazing. 

250ml Vegetable Glycerin (1 cup)
60ml Water (1/4 cup)
120g (1/2 cup)

Heat to almost boiling, reduce heat to lowest setting and continue to heat for 1 hour. Store in air tight container for 1 month, strain and store.

comments.text:
Per Chat-GPT:

When you bake with vanilla extract (or any alcohol-based flavoring), the alcohol does not instantly disappear. How much remains depends on time, temperature, and method of cooking:
	•	High heat + long baking time → most alcohol evaporates. For example, a standard cake baked at 350°F for 30–40 minutes will lose the majority of the alcohol.
	•	Quick cooking or low heat (like stove-top sauces, custards, or glazes) → more alcohol can remain.
	•	Studies by the USDA show that after 1 hour of baking, only about 25% or less of the alcohol is left; after 2+ hours, virtually none remains.

So in your cake:
	•	By the time it’s fully baked, the alcohol content is negligible—what’s left is the vanilla flavor.
